(a) Five marks: identify original cost; calculate loss 2500; divide loss by original cost; multiply by 100; give a valid exact or rounded percentage (one each). (b) Five marks: ratio sum 22; unit share 1.5; identify largest term 7; mass 10.5 kg; family D (one each). (a(i)) Simplify 7m − 2(5n − 4m) + 11n − 5m.

(a(ii)) Simplify (5x − 2y) − 2(4x − 3y).

(b) The sum of two numbers is 19 and their difference is 5. Find the numbers.

(b) Four marks: sum equation; difference equation; elimination/substitution step; both correct numbers (one each). Accept valid equivalent methods and apply reasonable follow-through without double-penalising one arithmetic slip.
questions.workedSolution: (i) 7m−10n+8m+11n−5m=10m+n. (ii) 5x−2y−8x+6y=−3x+4y. (b) Let u+v=19 and u−v=5; adding gives 2u=24, so u=12 and v=7.

questions.markIncrementProvenance: Independent whole-mark self-assessment rubric; official subpart weights are not asserted.
questions.markingGuide: Independent SomaSmart self-assessment rubric (not an official NECTA scheme). (a) Five marks: rearranged slope form; correct gradient equation; solve k=1; identify intercept expression 7/k; obtain intercept 7 (one each). (b) Five marks: substitute A; substitute B; solve M=1; solve K=1/2; verify both points (one each). Accept valid equivalent methods and apply reasonable follow-through without double-penalising one arithmetic slip.
questions.workedSolution: (a) For k≠0, y=((k+1)/k)x+7/k. Set (k+1)/k=2, giving k=1 and intercept 7. k=0 gives a vertical condition rather than the stated finite gradient. (b) −2K+5M=4 and 2K+3M=4; addition gives M=1, then K=1/2. Both source points satisfy the resulting line.

questions.answerKey: (a) y=28.2 cm. (b) A right triangle with vertical side 5 m, horizontal side 12 m and ladder as hypotenuse; ladder=13 m.
questions.markingGuide: Independent SomaSmart self-assessment rubric (not an official NECTA scheme). (a) Five marks: identify opposite side; sine ratio; rearrange to y=30sin70°; correct numerical evaluation; rounding and cm (one each). (b) Five marks: correctly labelled right-triangle sketch; Pythagorean equation; sum 169; square root 13; metres and interpretation of the sketch (one each). Accept valid equivalent methods and apply reasonable follow-through without double-penalising one arithmetic slip.
questions.workedSolution: (a) sin70°=y/30, so y=30sin70°≈28.1908 cm, giving 28.2 cm. (b) Interpreting the ladder as reaching the stated 5 m height, L²=5²+12²=169, so L=13 m. The wall and ground are perpendicular as the stated vertical/ground model requires.
